themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK—a 460% jump from the 1.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed operators or a coordinated enforcement gap in Greenwich Village/SoHo's high-traffic commercial zones.
evidence: 7 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.8)
Aligns with CB budget request for 'Other programs to address public health issues' suggesting recurring vendor enforcement challenges
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed vendors exploiting gaps in post-pandemic Department of Health enforcement?
Has a single vendor or network of vendors recently moved into the district, prompting complaints?

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Park-related noise complaints exploded to 9 THIS WEEK—a 227% spike from the 2.8 weekly average—concentrated in a district with heavy foot traffic and outdoor seating; investigate whether spring weather, new outdoor dining permits, or venue changes are driving disturbances.
evidence: 9 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.23)
District-wide noise complaints (all types) total 1,750 over 90 days—third-largest complaint category after illegal parking and heat/hot water
reporting_angles: Which parks (Washington Square, Hudson River Park waterfront) are the hotspots, and what events or venues are responsible?
Has the city issued new outdoor dining or event permits that residents weren't consulted on?

themes_detail.label: Tree Emergency Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying trees and illegal tree damage complaints combined for 9 complaints last week—with dead/dying trees UP 967% (4 vs. 0.4 weekly avg) and illegal damage UP 344% (5 vs. 1.1 weekly avg)—suggesting either storm damage, developer construction impacts, or a Parks Department backlog in tree maintenance that CB has requested funding for annually.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49—highest severity)
Illegal Tree Damage: 5 complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.96)
Community Board has requested 'Forestry services, including street tree maintenance' funding every year—unmet recurring need
reporting_angles: Did recent storms (or underground construction) trigger sudden tree die-offs or developer damage?
How long is Parks Department's response time for tree removal/replanting in Greenwich Village, and are budget constraints delaying action?

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 8 last week—a 300% spike from the 2.0 weekly average over 8 weeks—concentrated in a dense residential district with older walkup-to-luxury conversions; flagging potential building safety or maintenance crisis.
evidence: 8 elevator complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.37)
1,671 DOB filings in last 90 days (1,451 alterations) suggest ongoing renovation activity that may strain building systems
reporting_angles: Are landlords deferring elevator maintenance during renovation cycles to cut costs?
How many buildings in the district have elevators 20+ years old due for replacement, and what is DOB's inspection backlog?

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints hit 4 last week—a 357% spike from the 0.9 weekly average—indicating residents are mobilizing against unlicensed operators or licensed retailers violating local regulations in a newly-legalized market.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.0)
Suggests enforcement gap or rapid retail expansion residents are flagging to 311
reporting_angles: How many licensed cannabis retailers operate in Greenwich Village/SoHo, and are complaints targeting specific shops or unlicensed operators?
Is the city's cannabis licensing process keeping pace with demand in high-foot-traffic commercial areas?
